content: 1. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 2. Lasmiditan increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Serious interaction—use an alternative. 3. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 5. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions with CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 6. Lenolisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, leading to increased systemic exposure. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 8. Letermovir increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 14. Lithium and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Lofepramine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lomitapide levels may increase several folds. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 21. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 23. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The manufacturer recommends decreasing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Macimorelin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 milliseconds in the corrected QT interval. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this could increase the risk of torsades de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 29. Maprotiline and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 33. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Reduce the mavorixafor dose if needed. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It also decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 38. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of microbiota oral by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antibacterial agents may decrease the efficacy of microbiota oral. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with midazolam intranasal causes higher systemic exposure, which may prolong sedation. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Mipomersen and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs). Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Mirtazapine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Mitotane decreases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mitoxantrone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of mizolastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased plasma concentrations of momelotinib may elevate the risk of adverse reactions. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely.
